comment: Direct process.env reads outside the config layer. See #579 (guard repair) and #611 (the sweep). `entries` is a work queue and a ratchet: it may shrink, never grow. `exempt` records reads that cannot be routed through the config layer for a structural reason; each needs a written justification and is checked for staleness the same way, so it cannot outlive the code it describes.

exempt.reason: envUtils is BELOW the config layer, not outside it: runtimeConfig.ts imports getBooleanEnv/parseBooleanEnv/isFalsy/isFalsyExtended/isTruthy/isDebugOrVerbose/TRUTHY_OR_DEFAULT from it to do its own parsing. Routing this read through runtimeConfig would be a self-referential import cycle -- the loader would have to be loaded to answer a question it asks while loading. See the header comment in src/utils/envUtils.ts.

Same structural cycle as INDEX_SERVER_DEBUG above: read by isDebugOrVerbose(), which runtimeConfig.ts calls from parseLogLevel() while building the config object. The exemption is keyed per variable, not per file, so a NEW variable read added to envUtils still fails the guard.
